about: R-056's registry (tithe pass 2, A7): each golden and integration check of Katana with its oracle (what its expected side is and where it comes from), the test that shows it failing when the thing under test is wrong (its killer mutation), and what its verdict gates. test/ChecksTest.java holds every integration test and every test that reads a golden to an entry here; refuses an oracle whose path lies inside the module under test unless the entry says why it is independent anyway; checks each mutation names a test that exists; and checks each gate runs the test (the fast loop, or the pre-push suite whose --tests pattern selects it). A check it cannot hold is a finding, listed with the reason, never silent.

kinds.tool: a program outside Katana run on the same input (cobc, its layout, a second run)
kinds.file: data written by something other than the code under test (a published summary, a study's frozen output, a hash recorded by hand)
kinds.spec: a document a person wrote (IBM's rules, a table in docs/)
kinds.self: a golden written by the code it checks (`-Dkatana.record=true`): it catches change, not error

oracle.what: cobc, for which programs it accepts; the source text, for the source map's round trip

checks.finding: No test shows it failing: a parser that tagged no error node would pass it. The counts only rise (the ratchet), so a fall is caught, but an over-accepting parser is not.

checks.finding: A self golden of counts: it catches a reader that starts reading the same files differently, not one that reads them wrongly. The cases' meaning is refuted by running them under cobc (3.1's runner, to come; the trial passes 227 of 378, J-093).
